one_sentence_goal: Determine whether cross-round temporal signals (deviation-trace stability and inter-client correlation) can distinguish colluding Sybils from a legitimate non-IID majority, which no single-round aggregation rule can do.
last_session_summary: Completed the original 4-item validation plan. Fixed the §5.8 numerical defect (f32 catastrophic cancellation in `1 - collusion`, now f64) and found the fix does NOT resolve the failure it was blamed for. Fixed Finding 3 (DSS now combines through the base method, so wrapping a robust method can no longer regress it) — all 9 robust-base cells repaired. Built a harder collusion model (correlated, non-identical Sybils) which answered §5.6's open question and incidentally found FoolsGold degrades 5.6x against it. Ran the first real-data validation, which found Centered Clipping's default clip radius loses to no defense at all.
phase: post-validation; hypothesis partially supported, three open design questions

hypothesis_status.claim_2_non_iid_conflation: demonstrated empirically (§5.4), with a structural split between method families
hypothesis_status.dss_core_hypothesis: supported on ONE attack shape only (temporally unstable colluders, §5.5: fedavg 161.3 -> 1.18). Does not catch stable colluders, by its own design.
hypothesis_status.dss_safety_as_a_wrapper: resolved 2026-08-31 (§5.11). Was the most serious problem found; wrapping a robust base could regress it up to 577x. Now cannot do materially worse than what it wraps.
hypothesis_status.dss_under_solo_attacker: OPEN. Still fails with a fragile base. Cause isolated (§5.8.1): the shared deviation reference is itself unstable when the base method is. Design problem, not arithmetic.

what_changed_this_session: conflux-core/src/temporal.rs: collusion score computed in f64 (fixes catastrophic cancellation); DssAggregator gained `combine_through_base` (default true) which routes the combine through the wrapped base method
conflux-attacks: new CorrelatedSybilAttack (divergence=0 reproduces PersistentSybilAttack exactly)
run_experiment.rs: new `dssraw_` prefix (pre-Finding-3 combine, for A/B), `--clip-radius` flag, `correlated_sybil` and `correlated_sybil_unstable` attacks
New experiments 2.7 (Centered Clipping), 2.8 (Finding 3 fix), 2.9 (correlated Sybils), 3.1/3.2 (real-data MNIST)
conclusions_overturned_by_measurement: §5.8 predicted a mechanical epsilon fix would replace the chaotic regime with a predictable one. It did not: it made results reproducible (cross-seed CV 1.03 -> 0.43) but not better, and the §5.9 joint transient window came back byte-identical. The two did not share a root cause.
§5.8's specific prescribed fix (epsilon fallback at 1e-4*n) is measurably wrong -- it fires on a unit test with clean correct discrimination and returns the sybil-dominated mean.

§5.6 concluded the AND-gate was numerically identical to stability-only. That was an artifact of its identical-Sybil attack model. Against non-identical colluders, collusion-only scores 1.09 where stability-only scores 17.13.
§5.10 found a genuine clip-radius optimum at dim=3. It does not transfer: on a 50,890-parameter model the curve is monotonic toward FedAvg with no optimum anywhere.

reproducibility.known_gap: Real-data runs (3.1/3.2) are single-seed. Adequate for the negative result about clip_radius; not adequate for anything comparative.

environment.rust: cargo workspace, edition 2024; experiments are conflux-attacks examples
